title: Address moderate-interest debt
summary: Debt above your HYSA rate (~4–5%) but below your equity threshold (~6–7% after-tax). Includes some auto loans, some personal loans.
detailsHtml:
The middle zone

Debt in this range is neither emergency nor inert. The optimal allocation depends on whether you're maximizing tax-advantaged space yet and what your expected real return on investments looks like. A rough rule: if you're not yet maxing your IRA/HSA, the tax-advantaged investing wins. Once you're past the tax-advantaged stage, debt payoff in this range often beats taxable investing on a risk-adjusted basis.

The mortgage question

Mortgage rates above ~6% deserve to be evaluated in this category, despite the original flowchart's blanket exclusion. The decision is: rate (minus tax benefit if you itemize) versus expected real after-tax return on the alternative investment. For a 7.5% mortgage and an investor in the 24% bracket who doesn't itemize, the after-tax mortgage rate is the full 7.5% — higher than reasonable expected real returns. Prepaying makes sense. For a 3% mortgage, it almost never does.
